note: Dutch wall build-ups. Thicknesses are millimetres, listed from the outside in. `reviewed: true` means a person has signed the entry off; everything else is a draft drawn from Dutch practice and must be checked before anyone builds from it. Performance fields are present and deliberately empty: this extension does not compute or claim an Rc or U-value.

walls.source: The build-up this extension has shipped since openings 1.1; unchanged here, so a wall drawn before the library existed is the same wall.
The single-leaf partition this extension has shipped since openings 1.1; unchanged here.

Draft from current Dutch housing practice: a masonry outer leaf, a fully filled cavity, and a block inner leaf. To be checked against the BRG standard details and the Rc the Bouwbesluit asks for before it is marked reviewed.
Draft of a Dutch timber-frame build-up: timber cladding, a ventilated cavity, sheathing, an insulated stud zone, an installation void, and plasterboard.
walls.note: Two honest limits. The studs are not modelled: the 145 mm zone is counted as insulation, so its mass is the insulation's, not the frame's. And a vapour barrier is thinner than the 3 mm a skin may be, so it is not a layer here — it is part of the build-up, not of this stack.

walls.source: Draft: a 100 mm calcium-silicate block partition, the common Dutch non-loadbearing inner wall. To be checked against the block's actual format and the finish it gets on site.
Draft: a 200 mm calcium-silicate party wall between dwellings. The acoustic and fire requirements a party wall actually has to meet are not represented here — only its build-up.
